issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5.3 Appendix B, Between and Equal: Date/DateTime imprecision may make comparisons null; `DateTimeBetweenIsNull` example expects null for `@2012-01-01 between @2012-01-01T12 and @2012-01-02T12`.
issues.evidence: Fresh native/fallback probe translated `@2012-01-01 between @2012-01-01T12 and @2012-01-02T12` to `cqlSameOrAfter(...) AND cqlSameOrBefore(...)`. Native C++ returned NULL, forced Python fallback returned false. Expected: NULL.
issues.root_cause: The forced Python fallback temporal helper globally promoted full Date operands to midnight DateTime, so public comparison helpers returned false rather than NULL for precision-uncertain Date-vs-DateTime comparisons.
issues.resolution: Made public `_compare_at_min_precision` strict by default and added explicit `promote_date_to_datetime=True` only for interval boundary internals that need endpoint normalization.
issues.verified_in: Iteration 1 focused comparison/interval pytest, official comparison pytest, CMS2 native/fallback DQM, full conformance, full fhir4ds pytest

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5.3 Appendix B, Equivalent: Decimal equivalence compares values rounded to the precision of the least precise operand, ignoring trailing zeroes.
issues.evidence: Fresh native/fallback probe returned false for `3.54 ~ 3.5` and true for `3.54 !~ 3.5` because generic equivalence lowered to plain SQL equality (`3.54 = 3.5`). Expected: `3.54 ~ 3.5` true after rounding to one decimal place.
issues.root_cause: Static decimal equivalence fell through to raw SQL equality instead of applying CQL least-precise-operand rounding.
issues.resolution: Added static decimal literal equivalence lowering that derives authored precision and compares explicitly rounded values using CQL-safe floor/ceil scaling.
issues.verified_in: Iteration 1 focused comparison pytest, official comparison pytest, full conformance, full fhir4ds pytest

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5.3 Appendix B, Equal/Equivalent/Greater/Less for time-valued quantities: variable calendar duration conversion to definite durations returns null for equality/comparison; equivalence treats `1 year ~ 365 days` and `1 month ~ 30 days` as true.
issues.evidence: Fresh native/fallback probe returned false for `1 year = 365 days` instead of NULL, and false for `1 year ~ 365 days` instead of true. Public direct `quantityCompare` uses the same helper path in native C++ and forced Python fallback.
issues.root_cause: Quantity equality/comparison treated calendar and definite duration units as ordinary incompatible units, and equivalence reused equality semantics.
issues.resolution: Routed Quantity equivalence through `quantityCompare(..., '~')` and aligned Python fallback plus native C++ duration comparison logic for calendar-vs-definite NULL behavior and CQL duration equivalence factors.
issues.verified_in: Iteration 1 focused comparison pytest, native C++ unittest, official comparison pytest, full conformance, full fhir4ds pytest
